source_codes: Wireshark 4.6.9 value_strings (tshark -G values), which follow IEEE 802.11-2020/802.11be and RFC 3748

categories.INFRA: Infrastructure-level causes inferred from the air
categories.OTHER: Unclassified: goes to the discovery agent

entries.name: Network not broadcast on an AP radio
entries.plain: An access point advertises one of the site's networks but not the other, so devices that need it cannot find it there.
entries.signature: BSSID for SSID X heard from an AP whose other BSSIDs are heard on the same channel, but no beacon for SSID X from it.
entries.detect: For each AP (grouped by BSSID base), expected SSID set minus heard SSID set, over >= 60 s with the sensor alive.
entries.normal_lookalike: Network intentionally not deployed on that AP (needs config/inventory to rule out).
likely_causes: WLAN disabled on radio or AP group
standard_fix: re-apply WLAN profile to AP group

dataset.evidence: NET-C missing on AP03, AP13, AP16, AP17; NET-T missing on AP06, AP13, AP28 for all 30 min; the 8 NET-C devices homed on those APs never join.

entries.name: Access point silent
entries.plain: An access point that should exist is not heard at all.
entries.signature: No beacon from an expected AP on any monitored channel.
entries.detect: Expected AP list (inventory, or gap in AP numbering) minus APs heard, for >= 60 s.
entries.normal_lookalike: AP on a channel no sensor monitors.
likely_causes: AP moved to an unmonitored channel

dataset.evidence: AP13 never heard in 30 min on the 8 monitored channels (could be on an unmonitored channel).

entries.name: Probe storm
entries.plain: Devices search for networks far more than normal, flooding the air with questions and answers.
entries.signature: Probe requests/responses per client or per channel far above baseline; often many clients at once.
entries.detect: Probe responses per client > 1/s sustained 60 s, or area-wide probe traffic > 3x rolling baseline.
entries.normal_lookalike: A few background scans per client per minute; burst during a roam.
likely_causes: clients failing to connect keep scanning
confirm_outside_headers: check which clients are failing (link to EAP/KEY incidents)

dataset.evidence: 173,964 probe responses in 30 min, peak 13,015/min (217/s) in minute 3, falling as failing clients back off.

entries.name: Probe unanswered
entries.plain: Devices ask for a network and no access point answers.
entries.signature: Directed probe requests for SSID X with no probe response for X within 100 ms on that channel.
entries.detect: Unanswered directed probes per SSID per channel > 50% over 60 s.
entries.normal_lookalike: Client probing on a channel where the network is simply not deployed.
likely_causes: SSID not configured on local APs

entries.name: Beacon loss
entries.plain: The access point's heartbeat goes missing more than normal.
entries.signature: Beacon gaps of 2x..N x beacon interval for a BSSID while other BSSIDs are heard by the same sensor.
entries.detect: Loss > 10% for a BSSID over 60 s, sensor alive.
entries.normal_lookalike: ~1-3% loss at a distant sensor is normal.

dataset.evidence: Loss 1.7-2.3% on all 53 BSSIDs, max gap 0.41 s: below threshold, not an incident.

entries.name: Channel change / DFS event
entries.plain: An access point jumps to another channel, briefly disconnecting its devices.
entries.signature: Channel Switch Announcement element in beacons; BSSID disappears from one sensor and appears on another; mass deauth.
entries.detect: Any CSA element, or BSSID first-heard on a new channel after vanishing.
entries.normal_lookalike: Planned channel change in a maintenance window.
standard_fix: pin non-DFS channels for critical areas

dataset.evidence: 0 CSA elements, every BSSID stays on one channel.

entries.name: Beacon configuration drift
entries.plain: An access point changes what it advertises (security, rates, capabilities) without a planned change.
entries.signature: Hash of beacon elements for a BSSID changes over time.
entries.detect: Element hash change for a BSSID outside change window.
entries.normal_lookalike: Planned configuration push.

dataset.evidence: Not assessed: converter does not keep full element hash yet.

entries.name: Too many networks per channel
entries.plain: Too many networks share one radio lane, so their adverts crowd the air.
entries.signature: Count of BSSIDs beaconing on one channel.
entries.detect: > 6 BSSIDs per channel heard by one sensor.
likely_causes: too many APs on the same channel

dataset.evidence: 5-9 BSSIDs per channel; 9 on channels 36 and 40.

entries.name: 802.11 authentication rejected
entries.plain: The access point refuses the very first 'may I talk to you' step.
entries.signature: Authentication seq 2 with status != 0.
entries.detect: Any non-zero status on Authentication response; group by status.
entries.normal_lookalike: Single reject followed by success on another AP.

dataset.evidence: All 685 authentication responses status 0.

entries.name: 802.11 authentication timeout
entries.plain: A device asks to talk and never gets an answer.
entries.signature: Authentication seq 1 from client, no seq 2 from AP within 100 ms (repeated).
entries.detect: 3+ unanswered auth requests from one client in 10 s, AP otherwise alive.
entries.normal_lookalike: Sensor did not hear the AP's answer (check visibility).

entries.name: WPA3-SAE failure
entries.plain: Password-based WPA3 login fails.
entries.signature: SAE (auth alg 3) commit/confirm with non-zero status or repeated commits.
entries.detect: Status 76/77/123/126 or >= 3 SAE commit rounds without confirm.
entries.normal_lookalike: Anti-clogging token exchange (status 76) once is normal under load.

entries.name: Fast-transition (802.11r) authentication failure
entries.plain: A fast roam fails and the device has to do a full login.
entries.signature: Auth alg 2 (FT) with non-zero status, or reassoc with FT elements rejected.
entries.detect: Status 28/52/53/54/55 on FT auth/reassoc.

entries.name: Authentication flood
entries.plain: Many authentication attempts at once, overloading an access point.
entries.signature: Auth requests per AP far above baseline, many clients.
entries.detect: > 20 auth requests/s on one AP for 10 s.
entries.normal_lookalike: Shift start: many devices join at once (short burst).

entries.name: Association rejected: AP full / capacity
entries.plain: The access point says it cannot take more devices.
entries.signature: Association response status 17 (or 33, 93).
entries.detect: Any status 17/33/93; count per AP.
likely_causes: too many clients per radio at shift start

entries.name: Association rejected: capability or rate mismatch
entries.plain: The device does not support something the network requires.
entries.detect: Any such status.
likely_causes: basic rates set too high for device
confirm_outside_headers: device spec vs WLAN rate/capability profile
standard_fix: adjust WLAN profile or replace device

entries.name: Association rejected: PMF / temporary
entries.plain: The network requires protected management frames or asks the device to come back later.
entries.signature: Status 30 (try later) or 31 (robust management frame policy violation).
entries.detect: Status 31 any time; status 30 repeated without later success.
entries.normal_lookalike: One status 30 followed by success (PMF SA query) is normal.
standard_fix: set PMF optional for that SSID or update device

entries.name: Association rejected: security (RSN) mismatch
entries.plain: The device and network disagree on the security settings.
entries.signature: Status 40-46, 72.
entries.detect: Any such status.

entries.name: Association refused: policy or external reason
entries.plain: The access point refuses for a reason outside the Wi-Fi standard (policy, ACL, controller).
entries.detect: Any such status.

entries.name: Reassociation denied
entries.plain: A device moving between access points is refused.
entries.signature: Reassociation response status 11 (or non-zero).
entries.detect: Any non-zero reassoc status.
likely_causes: roam to AP that lost state

entries.name: Association timeout
entries.plain: A device asks to join and gets no answer.
entries.signature: Assoc request with no response within 100 ms, repeated.
entries.detect: 3+ unanswered assoc requests in 10 s.
entries.normal_lookalike: Response missed by sensor.

entries.name: QoS / traffic-stream request refused
entries.plain: A device's request for guaranteed bandwidth (voice/video stream) or a scheduled service was refused.
entries.signature: ADDTS/TS/scheduling responses with these statuses (Action frames).
entries.detect: Any such status; group by AP.
entries.normal_lookalike: Occasional refusals under load.

entries.name: Wi-Fi 7 multi-link / priority-access refused
entries.plain: A newer Wi-Fi 7 device could not join or use a link on a multi-link access point.
entries.detect: Any such status.

entries.name: Other advanced-feature refusal
entries.plain: A request for an optional feature (power save scheduling, fast session transfer, spectrum/energy features) was refused.
entries.signature: Statuses listed in codes.
entries.detect: Any such status; informational unless repeated for one client.
standard_fix: disable feature on client or enable on AP

entries.name: Passpoint / ANQP query failure
entries.plain: A device asking the network for service information (Hotspot 2.0) got no or a failed answer.
entries.signature: GAS/ANQP responses with these statuses.
entries.detect: Any such status.

entries.name: FILS authentication failure
entries.plain: Fast initial link setup (FILS) login failed.
entries.signature: Auth alg 4-6 with status 112/113.
entries.detect: Any such status.

entries.name: 802.1X stall after EAP Identity
entries.plain: The badge check never starts: the access point asks 'who are you?' and nothing happens after that.
entries.signature: Assoc OK, EAP Request/Identity from AP, optionally Response/Identity from client, then no EAP method request, no Success/Failure, no EAPOL M1; AP re-sends Identity request on a fixed timer.
entries.detect: No EAP method round within 20 s of Identity; confirm with >= 1 re-ask on a fixed interval.
entries.normal_lookalike: Slow but successful EAP (record as latency).

dataset.evidence: 654 NET-C join attempts by 63 devices on 26 APs, 0 EAP method rounds, 0 Success/Failure, 0 M1; re-ask median 30.0 s; 12 devices seen answering Identity.

entries.name: 802.1X stall mid-method
entries.plain: The badge check starts but stops half way.
entries.signature: EAP method rounds (TLS/PEAP) start, then stop without Success/Failure.
entries.detect: Last EAP frame is a method request/response and nothing follows for 20 s.
entries.normal_lookalike: Large TLS certificate chains take several rounds (slow, not stuck).

entries.name: EAP Failure
entries.plain: The badge server explicitly says no.
entries.signature: EAP code 4 (Failure).
entries.detect: Any EAP Failure; group by client.

dataset.evidence: 0 EAP Failure frames.

entries.name: Kicked out: 802.1X authentication failed (reason 23)
entries.plain: The access point throws the device out because the badge check failed or timed out.
entries.signature: Deauthentication reason 23 from AP.
entries.detect: Any reason 23; link to EAP-01/02/03 for cause.

dataset.evidence: 506 reason-23 deauths; 488 of 489 measured exactly 60.0 s after association.

entries.name: Client does not answer EAP Identity
entries.plain: The device never replies to 'who are you?'.
entries.signature: Repeated EAP Request/Identity with no Response/Identity while client frames are otherwise heard.
entries.detect: 3+ Identity requests unanswered while the sensor hears that client.
entries.normal_lookalike: Sensor cannot hear that client's uplink (check visibility first).
standard_fix: deploy correct Wi-Fi profile to device

dataset.evidence: 51 NET-C devices never heard answering, but 0 of their own join frames are heard either (vs ~48 each for the 12 that are heard answering): a visibility gap, not evidence.

entries.name: Slow 802.1X
entries.plain: Login works but takes too long, delaying the device every time it connects.
entries.signature: Identity -> Success > 2 s.
entries.detect: Median EAP duration per SSID > 2 s over 10 attempts.

entries.name: EAPOL-Start storm
entries.plain: Devices keep restarting the badge check.
entries.signature: Many EAPOL-Start frames from clients.
entries.detect: > 3 EAPOL-Start per client per minute.

entries.name: EAP method mismatch (NAK)
entries.plain: Device and server cannot agree on the badge-check method.
entries.signature: EAP Response type 3 (Legacy Nak).
entries.detect: Any Nak followed by failure/timeout.
entries.normal_lookalike: One Nak then agreement is normal.
likely_causes: server offers TLS, client wants PEAP (or vice versa)

entries.name: 4-way handshake: M2 never arrives (wrong key suspected)
entries.plain: The access point starts handing out the locker key but the device never answers correctly.
entries.signature: EAPOL M1 repeated (replay counter increments) with no M3; often ends with reason 15 or 2.
entries.detect: M1 sent >= 2 times without M3 within 5 s.
entries.normal_lookalike: One M1 retransmit then M3.

dataset.evidence: All 32 M1s to IoT are single; 31 followed by M3 in 0.3-2.5 ms.

entries.name: 4-way handshake: M4 missing / keys not installed
entries.plain: The device got the key but never confirmed it.
entries.signature: M3 repeated, no protected data afterwards, reason 15.
entries.detect: M3 sent >= 2 times without data or M4.
entries.normal_lookalike: M4 not heard by this sensor but data follows.

entries.name: MIC failure
entries.plain: The integrity check fails, often a wrong key or tampering.
entries.signature: Deauth reason 14, or M2 followed by M1 retransmit (bad MIC).
entries.detect: Any reason 14.

entries.name: Group key handshake timeout
entries.plain: Devices miss the shared broadcast key update and drop.
entries.signature: Deauth reason 16.
entries.detect: Any reason 16; cluster by time (GTK rekey interval).

entries.name: Security element mismatch in handshake
entries.plain: Security details differ between advert and handshake (possible downgrade).
entries.signature: Deauth reason 17-22, 24.
entries.detect: Any such reason.

entries.name: Handshake step not observed (visibility gap)
entries.plain: A handshake message was not captured, but later frames prove the step happened; not a failure.
entries.signature: M1 seen, M3 not seen, but AP continues the association (e.g. Block-Ack setup) and no failure reason follows.
entries.detect: Emit as info only; never as an incident.

dataset.evidence: 1 IoT join: M1 then Block-Ack setup from AP 60 ms later, no deauth; M3 simply not captured.

entries.name: Join-fail-kick loop
entries.plain: A device keeps trying to connect, fails, is thrown out, waits and tries again, over and over.
entries.signature: >= 3 cycles of association -> failure/deauth for one client within 10 min.
entries.detect: Count cycles per client; one incident per client, linked to cause.
entries.normal_lookalike: A single deauth during a roam.

dataset.evidence: 63 NET-C devices, 654 cycles; backoff grows from ~28 s (first 5 min) to ~200 s (after 20 min).

entries.name: Fast reject / client exclusion (reason 2 repeated)
entries.plain: After several failures the network starts throwing the device out within seconds of every attempt, and keeps repeating it.
entries.signature: Repeated deauth or disassoc reason 2 from AP to one client every ~10-30 s; each rejoin rejected within seconds; no more reason 23.
entries.detect: >= 3 reason-2 deauth/disassoc to one client within 2 min.
entries.normal_lookalike: One reason-2 after an AP-side state reset.
likely_causes: controller client-exclusion / block-list after repeated 802.1X failures
confirm_outside_headers: controller excluded-client list and its timer
standard_fix: clear exclusion after fixing root cause

dataset.evidence: 18 laptops (on 18 APs) switch after 3-5 reason-23 kicks, from 402 s to 641 s; 1,477 reason-2 frames at ~11-15 s (deauth) or ~26 s (disassoc) intervals; 0 reason-23 afterwards.

entries.name: Idle / inactivity disconnect
entries.plain: The network drops a device it thinks is idle.
entries.signature: Deauth/disassoc reason 4.
entries.detect: Many reason 4 on devices that are expected to stay online.
entries.normal_lookalike: Idle laptops overnight.
likely_causes: idle timeout too short for IoT
standard_fix: raise idle timeout for device class

entries.name: Disconnected because AP is full
entries.plain: The access point drops devices because it is overloaded.
entries.signature: Reason 5 or 33.
entries.detect: Any.

entries.name: State mismatch frames (class 2/3)
entries.plain: The device and access point disagree about whether the device is connected.
entries.signature: Deauth reason 6/7/9.
entries.detect: > 3 per client in 5 min.
entries.normal_lookalike: One after an AP reboot.

entries.name: Steered away (BSS transition)
entries.plain: The network pushes the device to another access point.
entries.signature: Reason 12, or BTM action frames.
entries.detect: Frequent BTM disconnects for the same client.
entries.normal_lookalike: Occasional band/load steering.

entries.name: Disconnected for poor radio conditions
entries.plain: The link got too bad and the network dropped the device.
entries.signature: Reason 34 or 71.
entries.detect: Any.

entries.name: Mass leave burst
entries.plain: Many devices disconnect within seconds, pointing to a shared trigger.
entries.signature: >= 8 distinct clients send leave/deauth within 10 s.
entries.detect: Count distinct clients per 10 s window.
entries.normal_lookalike: End of shift.

dataset.evidence: 15 devices (6 laptops, 5 phones, 4 IoT) sent reason 3 within 9 s at start.

entries.name: Normal leave (not an incident)
entries.plain: A device says goodbye on its own: normal behaviour.
entries.signature: Deauth/disassoc reason 3 or 8 from the client, no repeat.
entries.detect: Record only; never an incident unless part of SESS-01/08.

dataset.evidence: 16 reason-3 frames from clients.

entries.name: Unspecified disconnect
entries.plain: Disconnected with no reason given.
entries.signature: Reason 1.
entries.detect: Cluster by AP/client.

entries.name: QoS / session-policy disconnect
entries.plain: Disconnected for a QoS, service-provider or access-policy reason.
entries.detect: Any.

entries.name: Mesh-link events
entries.plain: Mesh backhaul peering problems (only on mesh deployments).
entries.signature: Reasons 52-68.
entries.detect: Any.

entries.name: Normal roam (not an incident)
entries.plain: A device moves to a better access point: normal.
entries.signature: Leave on AP A then (re)assoc on AP B within ~1 s.
entries.detect: Record roam latency only.

dataset.evidence: No device changed AP in 30 min.

entries.name: Slow roam
entries.plain: Moving between access points takes too long and breaks connections.
entries.signature: Roam gap > 150 ms (voice) / > 1 s (data).
entries.detect: Median roam gap per SSID above threshold.

entries.name: Sticky client
entries.plain: A device stays on a far, weak access point instead of moving to a closer one.
entries.signature: RSSI of client at its AP falling, retries rising, while a stronger AP is heard by the same sensor.
entries.detect: Signal < -75 dBm for 60 s with a >= 8 dB better AP available.
entries.normal_lookalike: Stationary device with a steady weak link.

entries.name: Ping-pong roaming
entries.plain: A device keeps bouncing between two access points.
entries.signature: >= 4 roams between the same two APs in 5 min.
entries.detect: Count A<->B transitions per client.

entries.name: Missing acknowledgements / high retries
entries.plain: Many messages are not acknowledged and have to be sent again.
entries.signature: Retry flag share per transmitter/frame type; retransmit of same seq.
entries.detect: Retry share > 20% (>= 30 frames) per transmitter or frame type.
entries.normal_lookalike: Short burst during a roam.

dataset.evidence: 31.3% of probe responses retried (54,484); 60 other retries in 1.1 M frames.

entries.name: Channel congestion
entries.plain: The radio lane is too busy.
entries.signature: High airtime use from frame durations and rates; many BSS per channel.
entries.detect: Estimated airtime > 50% for 60 s.

dataset.evidence: Airtime estimate low except beacon overhead (see RF-03).

entries.name: Beacon overhead
entries.plain: Access point adverts use a big share of the air before any useful work.
entries.signature: Sum of beacon airtime per channel.
entries.detect: > 10% at stated rate.

dataset.evidence: 10-19% per channel at the stated 1 Mbit/s; 1.7-3% if 6 Mbit/s.

entries.name: Basic rate too low / legacy rate
entries.plain: Management frames are sent at a very slow rate, wasting air.
entries.signature: Beacon/mgmt rate at lowest rate of the band (or invalid for band).
entries.detect: Any beacon rate < 12 Mbit/s on 5 GHz.

dataset.evidence: All 914,057 beacons at 1 Mbit/s on 5 GHz.

entries.name: Weak client signal
entries.plain: Devices are too far from the access point.
entries.signature: Client RSSI at sensor near AP < -80 dBm (needs sensor near AP).
entries.detect: Per-client RSSI trend.

dataset.evidence: Clients heard at -80..-89 dBm but sensors are not co-located with APs, so this is not a valid client-signal measure.

entries.name: Co-channel overlap
entries.plain: Neighbouring access points share the same lane and slow each other down.
entries.signature: Several APs on one channel heard at similar strength by one sensor.
entries.detect: >= 3 APs within 6 dB on one channel.

dataset.evidence: Up to 5 APs on one channel; physical distances unknown (no map).

entries.name: High noise floor
entries.plain: Background radio noise makes everything slower.
entries.signature: radiotap noise > -85 dBm sustained.
entries.detect: Median noise > -85 dBm over 60 s.

entries.name: Power-save misbehaviour
entries.plain: Sleepy devices miss messages and drop.
entries.signature: PS bit toggling rapidly; group-key timeouts.
entries.detect: > 10 PS toggles/s per client.

entries.name: Null-data keepalive storm
entries.plain: A device sends too many 'still here' frames.
entries.signature: Null/QoS-Null frames per client per second.
entries.detect: > 5/s sustained.

dataset.evidence: QoS Null frames present at low rate from IoT.

entries.name: Deauthentication flood / spoofed deauth
entries.plain: Someone may be forcing devices off the network.
entries.signature: Many deauths (often broadcast) with sequence numbers inconsistent with the AP's own counter.
entries.detect: > 20 deauth/s or seq jumps vs AP's frames.
entries.normal_lookalike: Legitimate controller mass-deauth during change.

dataset.evidence: Reason-2 deauths carry the AP's own increasing sequence numbers at 10-30 s per client: sent by the AP itself (SESS-02), not a spoofed flood.

entries.name: Rogue / evil-twin AP
entries.plain: An unknown access point advertises the company network.
entries.signature: Beacon with corporate SSID from a BSSID not in the inventory / other vendor OUI.
entries.detect: Any unknown BSSID with a corporate SSID.
entries.normal_lookalike: New AP not yet in inventory.

dataset.evidence: All 53 BSSIDs share one vendor OUI.

entries.name: Protected management frames not enforced
entries.plain: Management frames are not protected, making spoofed disconnects possible.
entries.signature: RSN capabilities MFPR=0 on corporate SSID.
entries.detect: Beacon RSN MFPR bit.
standard_fix: require PMF where clients support it

dataset.evidence: Not assessed: converter does not extract RSN capability bits yet.

entries.name: Central authentication service outage
entries.plain: The same login failure happens on many access points at once, so the cause is a shared service behind them.
entries.signature: EAP-01/EAP-03 on >= 3 APs or >= 2 channels within 2 min, while another SSID on the same radios is healthy.
entries.detect: Root-incident rule over EAP incidents + control comparison.

dataset.evidence: EAP-01 on 26 APs, 8 channels, 8 sensors; NET-T on same radios: 31 handshakes, 0 failures. Streaming detector would fire at 47.5 s.

entries.name: AP reboot
entries.plain: An access point restarted.
entries.signature: Beacons stop then resume with TSF reset near zero.
entries.detect: Beacon gap > 5 s then TSF < previous.

entries.name: Controller-wide behaviour change
entries.plain: Many APs change behaviour at the same moment (config push).
entries.signature: Same new pattern (e.g. new reason code) starts on many APs within a short window.
entries.detect: New reason/status code on >= 3 APs within 60 s.

dataset.evidence: SESS-02 onset is a rolling 15 s-per-client wave (402-641 s), not simultaneous.

entries.name: Sensor deaf / silent
entries.plain: A sensor stops hearing anything.
entries.signature: No beacons from any AP for > 2 s.
entries.detect: Gap > 2 s in all beacons for a sensor.

dataset.evidence: Longest beacon gap 0.41 s on any sensor.

entries.name: Sensor clock offset
entries.plain: Sensors' clocks disagree, so matching events across sensors needs tolerance.
entries.signature: Same scripted/periodic event lines up on per-sensor relative time but not on wall-clock time.
entries.detect: Estimate offset from shared BSSID TSF when available.

dataset.evidence: Start epochs differ by up to 2.3 s; joins sit on an exact 2 s grid in per-sensor time only. Cannot tell offset from staggered start (no shared BSSID).

entries.name: Partial capture window
entries.plain: The analysed data covers only part of the recording.
entries.signature: Converted window << capture length.
entries.detect: Compare window to capture length.

dataset.evidence: Old JSON: 50 s of 1,802 s (2.8%).

entries.name: Physically impossible radio values
entries.plain: The capture contains values real radios cannot produce.
entries.signature: e.g. 1 Mbit/s on 5 GHz, constant RSSI.
entries.detect: Rate not valid for band; RSSI variance 0 across > 100 frames.

dataset.evidence: 1 Mbit/s beacons on 5 GHz; RSSI constant on 53/53 BSSIDs.

entries.name: Uplink not heard (visibility asymmetry)
entries.plain: Sensors hear access points far better than devices, so many device frames are missing.
entries.signature: Ratio of AP-sent to client-sent frames in handshakes.
entries.detect: Track per-client visibility; lower confidence of client-side verdicts.

dataset.evidence: 173,964 probe responses vs 6,024 probe requests; M2/M4 heard for 4 of 24 IoT devices.

entries.name: Truncated frames
entries.plain: Frames are cut to headers (by design); lengths must use the on-air size.
entries.signature: caplen < frame length.
entries.detect: Informational.

dataset.evidence: Data frames truncated (e.g. 49 of 137 bytes).

entries.name: Unknown or unmapped code
entries.plain: A status/reason/EAP code arrived that the catalog does not map (reserved or vendor-specific).
entries.signature: Code value not in ieee_codes.json or not mapped to an entry.
entries.detect: Every such frame -> unknown_events.jsonl.

entries.name: Unexpected sequence
entries.plain: Frames arrived in an order no known pattern explains.
entries.signature: Episode state machine hits an undefined transition.
entries.detect: Every such transition -> unknown_events.jsonl.

entries.name: Statistical anomaly
entries.plain: A metric moved far from normal with no known explanation.
entries.signature: Per-metric z-score > 4 vs rolling baseline, no catalog detector fired.
entries.detect: Every such spike -> unknown_events.jsonl.

5.text: Disassociated because AP is unable to handle all currently associated STAs

6.text: Class 2 frame received from nonauthenticated STA

7.text: Class 3 frame received from nonassociated STA

11.text: Disassociated because the information in the Supported Channels element is unacceptable

12.text: Disassociated due to BSS transition management

13.text: Invalid information element, i.e., an information element defined in this standard for which the content does not meet the specifications in Clause 9

17.text: Element in 4-way handshake different from (Re)Association Request/Probe Response/Beacon frame

24.text: Cipher suite rejected because of the security policy

25.text: TDLS direct-link teardown due to TDLS peer STA unreachable via the TDLS direct link

26.text: TDLS direct-link teardown for unspecified reason

27.text: Disassociated because session terminated by SSP request

28.text: Disassociated because of lack of SSP roaming agreement

29.text: Requested service rejected because of SSP cipher suite or AKM requirement

30.text: Requested service not authorized in this location

31.text: TS deleted because QoS AP lacks sufficient bandwidth for this QoS STA due to a change in BSS service characteristics or operational mode

33.text: Disassociated because QoS AP lacks sufficient bandwidth for this QoS STA

34.text: Disassociated because excessive number of frames need to be acknowledged, but are not acknowledged due to AP transmissions and/or poor channel conditions

35.text: Disassociated because STA is transmitting outside the limits of its TXOPs

36.text: Requested from peer STA as the STA is leaving the BSS (or resetting)

37.text: Requesting STA is no longer using the stream or session

38.text: Requesting STA received frames using a mechanism for which a setup has not been completed

39.text: Requested from peer STA due to timeout

46.text: Disassociated because authorized access limit reached

47.text: Disassociated due to external service requirements
